day_shape: 99 items: UK attributes RAF Fairford plot to IRGC with 29-country joint statement and two sanctions designations, Rubio-Miliband reaffirm Strait of Hormuz commitment after UKMTO logs 12 tanker incidents in a week, Houthi drones hit Riyadh, and Zahedan clashes leave at least six dead.

threads.label: UK attributes RAF Fairford plot to IRGC
threads.summary: Britain said the IRGC “almost certainly” directed a suspected attack plot on RAF Fairford, sanctioned two Iranian nationals and summoned Tehran's ambassador. A joint statement from 29 foreign ministries, coordinated via the US State Department, condemned Iranian state-sponsored violence abroad; Iran denied involvement.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz shipping and diplomacy
threads.summary: Secretary Rubio and UK Foreign Secretary Miliband reaffirmed commitment to safeguarding Strait of Hormuz transit, and UKMTO reported a products tanker struck by an unknown projectile and 12 commercial-ship incidents between 5–11 October. OFAC published an Iran-related sector determination in the Federal Register; Iran International reported hardliners endorsing Mohsen Rezaei's threat to strike Persian Gulf data centres and subsea cables.

threads.label: Yemen-Saudi exchange and US posture
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press reported Houthi drone strikes on Riyadh with three explosions reported in the north and claims that Saudi early-warning systems failed at King Khalid airport, while the Saudi-led coalition issued evacuation warnings for a Sanaa fuel facility. The Jerusalem Post reported Houthi threats of a “swift and painful response” if Washington joins the Saudi campaign, Iran offering to mediate, and Trump dismissing claims of Chinese and Russian help to Tehran.

threads.label: Sistan-Baluchestan clashes escalate
threads.summary: Iran International, citing HRANA, reported at least 94 killed and 33 wounded in southeastern Iran since 31 March, with the IRGC saying five alleged kidnappers and one guard were killed near Zahedan. Defa Press reported a terrorist safe house destroyed in Chah Ahmad Kurin and IRIB said a kidnapping cell was dismantled by IRGC Ground Forces' Quds HQ.

threads.label: Northern Israel ordnance and Lebanon
threads.summary: A 9th grader, Elazar Yair Wilensky, was named as the student killed by a Hezbollah cluster submunition on a school trip near the Lebanon border; Netanyahu met the wounded and IDF Chief of Staff Zamir ordered an investigation. The IDF expanded a public awareness campaign on unexploded ordnance, launched an interceptor at a suspicious aerial target over southern Lebanon, and assessed an earlier Galilee UFO as likely a balloon.

threads.label: IDF Gaza and West Bank operations
threads.summary: The IDF said five Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives were killed in strikes in southern Gaza, naming three PIJ members including engineering operative Muhammad Abu Hajjaj and two Nukhba terrorists. Troops acting on Shin Bet intelligence apprehended four PIJ operatives in Qabatiya and Arraba in the northern West Bank who allegedly planned an attack.

threads.label: Iran posture, Trump remarks and WSJ warnings
threads.summary: The Wall Street Journal, cited by Iran International, reported Iranian officials privately warned of possible land incursions into neighbouring countries if the US resumes strikes, while the Jerusalem Post said Trump suggested Washington may have gone “too far” in targeting Iran's leadership. Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi thanked Russia's president for offering mediation, and government spokesman Mohajjerani said Tehran is prepared for “the harshest war scenarios.”

events.summary_en: Hackers carried out a cyber attack on hundreds of chain stores in France and manipulated cooling systems, causing widespread food spoilage and fires in several stores that resulted in tens of millions of dollars in damage. French news agencies reported that hundreds of supermarkets in France were targeted in a large-scale cyber attack. During the attack, store cooling management systems were remotely manipulated and temperatures in fridges and freezers were raised to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), leading to food spoilage and fires in multiple stores.
